info.name: Field Service Management API
info.description:
# Field Service Management API

Postman collection for the Field Service Management backend (`/api/v1`).

## Setup (2 minutes)
1. Open the **Variables** tab of this collection.
2. Set `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:5000/api/v1`).
3. Fill the **password** variables with the values from your `.env` (seeded accounts: super admin, admin, manager, technician). Emails are pre-filled with the example values, change them if yours differ.
4. Run the requests in **0. Login** for the roles you need.

Every request already uses the token of its role (`customerToken`, `managerToken`, ...), so you can jump between roles without logging in again. IDs (`serviceRequestId`, `assignmentId`, `workOrderId`, `paymentId`...) are saved automatically by test scripts.

## Happy path (in this order)
| # | Role | Request |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Customer | 1. Auth → Register customer → Verify email (OTP from email) |
| 2 | Manager | 3. Skills → Create skill |
| 3 | Customer | 5. Service Requests → Create service request |
| 4 | Manager | Mark under review → Review: APPROVE |
| 5 | Manager | 6. Assignments → Available technicians → Create assignment |
| 6 | Technician | Confirm assignment (creates the work order) |
| 7 | Manager | 7. Work Orders → Get work orders of a request (saves `workOrderId`) |
| 8 | Technician | En route → Arrived → Start work → Add part → Service report → Complete work |
| 9 | Manager | Verify work order |
| 10 | Manager | 8. Payments → Create invoice |
| 11 | Customer / Manager | Initiate bKash payment, or Mark paid in cash |
| 12 | Customer | 9. Feedback → Create feedback |

## Notes
- The API accepts the token from a cookie **or** the `Authorization: Bearer` header, and prefers the cookie. A collection pre-request script clears cookies so the per-role Bearer token is always used.
- Technician needs to be **approved** (4. Technicians → Review application) and **available** before they can be assigned.
- Time slots for assignments are generated automatically (tomorrow, 2 hours).

exec: // The API reads the accessToken COOKIE before the Authorization header.
// Clear cookies so the per-role Bearer token on each request is always the one used.

request.description:
**Access:** Public (no login)

Logs in and stores the token in `customerToken`. Every request of the matching role uses this token automatically.

Set `customerEmail` and `customerPassword` in the collection **Variables** tab first.

exec: pm.test('Logged in, token saved to customerToken', () => pm.expect(body.data.accessToken).to.be.a('string'));
